key_insight: APOE associations with dementia, liver disease and plasma proteins varied by ancestry, while SNAP25 increased with APOE ε4 dosage across ancestries.
clinical_relevance: The findings support ancestry-aware research on APOE-related risk and biomarkers, but do not establish clinical tests or treatment recommendations.
method: Tested APOE genotype associations with 2,632 phenotypes in 367,757 All of Us participants across six genetic ancestry groups.
Adjusted for demographic and genetic covariates and assessed sex- and ancestry-related heterogeneity.
Evaluated APOE ε2 and ε4 dosage associations with plasma proteins in 9,132 participants across five ancestries.
evidence_signal: The study identified 27 associated phenotypes, including nine associations with ancestry-specific effects and five lipid-related traits with larger effects in females.
watch_item: These observational associations require independent validation; this is APOE target-biology research, not an AI cancer drug discovery study.
paper_title: Phenome-wide and proteomic analysis of APOE alleles across different ancestries in the All of Us Research Program
